questions.q: A 35-year-old farmer presents with a painless ulcer on the dorsum of the right hand with a black necrotic centre and surrounding oedema. He works with animal hides. The most likely causative organism is:
questions.exp: Cutaneous anthrax (malignant pustule) presents as a painless black eschar with surrounding gelatinous non-pitting oedema. It is caused by Bacillus anthracis and is an occupational hazard for those handling animal products.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman presents with painful grouped vesicles on an erythematous base over the right buttock. She had a similar episode 6 months ago at the same site. The treatment of choice for suppression of recurrences is:
questions.exp: Suppressive therapy for recurrent genital herpes (HSV-2) uses Acyclovir 400 mg twice daily for 6–12 months, which reduces frequency and severity of recurrences and reduces viral shedding.

questions.q: A 22-year-old male presents with annular scaly patches on the trunk with central clearing. KOH preparation shows branched hyphae with arthroconidia. The most appropriate treatment is:
questions.exp: Tinea corporis with hyphae on KOH is treated with terbinafine 250 mg once daily for 2–4 weeks. Terbinafine is fungicidal and the preferred agent for dermatophytosis; griseofulvin requires longer courses and is fungistatic.

questions.q: A 40-year-old male presents with hypopigmented anaesthetic patches on the trunk and thickened great auricular nerve. Slit-skin smear shows acid-fast bacilli. Which leprosy type does this most likely represent?
questions.exp: Lepromatous leprosy (LL) is characterised by numerous bacilli on smear (high bacterial index), diffuse infiltration, and thickened peripheral nerves. Tuberculoid has few or no bacilli and well-defined lesions. BL has more bacilli than BB, but diffuse multiple lesions with AFB smear positivity points to LL.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman with systemic lupus erythematosus develops a butterfly rash, oral ulcers, and photosensitivity. The autoantibody most specific for SLE is:
questions.exp: Anti-Sm (anti-Smith) is the most specific antibody for SLE (specificity ~99%), though less sensitive (~25–30%). Anti-dsDNA has high specificity and correlates with disease activity. Anti-histone is associated with drug-induced lupus. Anti-Ro/SSA is seen in Sjögren's syndrome and subacute cutaneous LE.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with tense bullae on normal-appearing skin and urticarial plaques. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 at the dermo-epidermal junction. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid shows tense subepidermal bullae, urticarial plaques in older patients, and linear IgG/C3 at the BMZ on DIF. Target antigens are BP180 and BP230. Pemphigus shows flaccid bullae with suprabasal split and IgG in intercellular space. DH shows granular IgA at dermal papillae tips. Linear IgA shows linear IgA at BMZ.

questions.q: A 25-year-old male presents with well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scales over the extensor surfaces and scalp. Nail pitting is present. The pathological hallmark seen on histopathology is:
questions.exp: Munro microabscesses (collections of neutrophils in the stratum corneum) are pathognomonic of psoriasis. Pautrier microabscesses (atypical lymphocytes in the epidermis) are seen in mycosis fungoides. Civatte bodies are found in lichen planus. Kamino bodies (eosinophilic globules) are characteristic of Spitz naevus.

questions.q: A 30-year-old HIV-positive male develops molluscum contagiosum-like lesions on the face which fail to respond to standard treatment. On histology, the organisms are PAS-positive and show narrow-based budding. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Disseminated cryptococcosis in HIV patients presents with skin lesions resembling molluscum contagiosum. Histology shows encapsulated yeasts with narrow-based budding that are PAS positive. Talaromyces (Penicillium) marneffei shows intracellular organisms with a transverse septum; Histoplasma shows small intracellular yeasts.

questions.q: A 20-year-old woman presents with itchy papulovesicles in the web spaces of fingers, wrists, and periumbilical area. Similar lesions are present in three family members. The treatment of choice is:
opts: Benzyl benzoate 25% applied for 24 hours once
questions.exp: Scabies (caused by Sarcoptes scabiei) is the most likely diagnosis in this clinical scenario with household contacts affected. Permethrin 5% cream is the treatment of choice — applied from neck down, left overnight, washed off after 8–14 hours; repeated after 1 week. All household contacts should be treated simultaneously.

questions.q: A 32-year-old male presents with a painless indurated ulcer on the glans penis for 3 weeks. VDRL is reactive. Which stage of syphilis does this represent?
questions.exp: A painless indurated ulcer (chancre) at the site of inoculation characterises primary syphilis, typically appearing 10–90 days after exposure. VDRL may be reactive at this stage but can also be negative early. Secondary syphilis presents weeks later with mucocutaneous rash, condylomata lata, and lymphadenopathy.

questions.q: A 50-year-old male with a 30-year history of plaque psoriasis develops erythroderma. The most dangerous immediate complication of erythrodermic psoriasis is:
questions.exp: Erythroderma causes massive peripheral vasodilation leading to high-output cardiac failure, the most dangerous acute complication especially in patients with pre-existing cardiac disease. The massive increase in skin blood flow increases cardiac workload significantly. Other complications include hypothermia, hypoalbuminaemia, and sepsis.

questions.q: A neonate presents on day 2 of life with superficial flaccid bullae that rupture leaving collarettes of scale. Gram stain shows Gram-positive cocci in clusters. The causative toxin acts on:
questions.exp: Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome (SSSS) is caused by exfoliative toxins A and B from S. aureus, which cleave desmoglein-1 (a desmosomal cadherin) in the granular layer of the epidermis, leading to superficial blister formation. Desmoglein-3 is targeted in pemphigus vulgaris.

questions.q: A 38-year-old woman presents with progressive thickening of skin on the fingers, Raynaud's phenomenon, and dysphagia. ANA is positive. Which antibody pattern is most specific for diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis?
questions.exp: Anti-Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase I) is associated with diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis and carries a higher risk of interstitial lung disease. Anti-centromere antibody is associated with limited cutaneous SSc (CREST syndrome). Anti-RNA polymerase III is associated with diffuse SSc and renal crisis. Anti-U1-RNP is associated with mixed connective tissue disease.

questions.q: A 60-year-old farmer presents with a nodule on the dorsum of the left hand with satellite nodules along the lymphatics of the forearm. KOH preparation is negative. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Sporotrichosis (Sporothrix schenckii) presents as a classic sporotrichoid or lymphocutaneous pattern — a primary nodule followed by satellite nodules along lymphatics. Chromoblastomycosis presents as verrucous plaques, mycetoma shows swelling with sinuses and grains, and cutaneous leishmaniasis presents as a non-healing ulcer.

questions.q: A 70-year-old male with actinic keratoses on the scalp presents with a rapidly growing keratotic nodule with a central keratin-filled crater. The lesion involuted spontaneously in 3 months. This is most consistent with:
questions.exp: Keratoacanthoma is a rapidly growing crateriform nodule with a central keratin plug that typically involutes spontaneously within 3–6 months. It is considered by many a low-grade variant of SCC. SCC does not spontaneously involute and is more locally invasive. Merkel cell carcinoma and sebaceous carcinoma have different presentations.

questions.q: A 25-year-old female presents with multiple comedones, inflammatory papules, nodules, and scarring over the face, chest, and back for 3 years. She has failed multiple courses of antibiotics and topical retinoids. The most appropriate next step is:
questions.exp: Severe nodulocystic acne or acne resistant to multiple antibiotic courses is an indication for oral isotretinoin. It targets all four pathogenic factors of acne: sebum production, follicular keratinisation, P. acnes colonisation, and inflammation. It is the only treatment that can induce long-term remission.

questions.q: A 45-year-old male presents with necrobiosis lipoidica diabeticorum. The characteristic histological finding in this condition is:
opts: Palisading granulomas with necrobiosis of collagen
Tuberculoid granulomas with Langhans giant cells
questions.exp: Necrobiosis lipoidica shows palisading histiocytes surrounding areas of degenerated collagen (necrobiosis) in the dermis, extending into the subcutis. This pattern distinguishes it from sarcoidosis (sarcoidal granulomas) and tuberculosis (caseating granulomas with Langhans cells).

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman presents with a pruritic eruption over the elbows, knees, and buttocks. Direct immunofluorescence shows granular IgA deposits at the tips of dermal papillae. The associated systemic condition is:
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis is characterised by intensely pruritic papulovesicles over extensor surfaces with granular IgA deposits at dermal papillae tips on DIF. It is strongly associated with gluten-sensitive enteropathy (coeliac disease). Dapsone is the treatment of choice alongside a gluten-free diet.

questions.q: A 30-year-old man presents with painful, tender, erythematous nodules on both shins for 10 days. He had a sore throat 3 weeks ago. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum presents with bilateral tender erythematous nodules on the anterior shins, often following streptococcal pharyngitis. It represents a hypersensitivity reaction (septal panniculitis without vasculitis). Nodular vasculitis occurs on the posterior calf. PAN causes skin infarcts and livedo. Weber-Christian is a relapsing febrile panniculitis.

questions.q: During patch testing for contact dermatitis, a patient develops a reaction graded ++ at the site of a standard allergen. A ++ reaction in patch testing signifies:
questions.exp: Patch test grading (ICDRG criteria): + (weak) = erythema and infiltration; ++ (strong) = erythema, infiltration, papules, and vesicles; +++ (extreme) = erythema, infiltration, papules, coalescing vesicles/bullae. Erythema alone is doubtful (?+). Blistering and ulceration represent a +++ or extreme reaction.

questions.q: A 3-year-old child presents with honey-crusted lesions around the nose and mouth. Culture yields a Gram-positive organism sensitive to mupirocin. The primary treatment for localised impetigo is:
opts: Topical mupirocin 2% ointment TDS for 5-7 days
Topical fusidic acid cream once daily
questions.exp: Localised non-bullous impetigo is treated with topical antibiotics such as mupirocin 2% ointment three times daily for 5–7 days or retapamulin. Systemic antibiotics are reserved for widespread, bullous, or recurrent disease. Fusidic acid is an alternative topical agent but mupirocin has superior efficacy against S. aureus.

questions.q: A 40-year-old male presents with progressive patchy hair loss forming a band-like pattern over the parieto-temporal scalp. On dermoscopy, peripilar casts and follicular redness are noted. Biopsy shows lymphocytic infiltration around the bulge area. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Lichen planopilaris is the most common cause of primary cicatricial (scarring) alopecia. It presents with perifollicular erythema, follicular hyperkeratosis (peripilar casts on dermoscopy), and a lymphocytic interface dermatitis around the isthmus/bulge on histology. Folliculitis decalvans is neutrophilic; DLE shows IgM/IgG deposits on DIF.

questions.q: A 28-year-old male with recurrent oral ulcers, genital ulcers, and uveitis is diagnosed with Behçet's disease. The pathergy test is positive. The drug of choice for mucocutaneous lesions is:
questions.exp: Colchicine is the first-line treatment for mucocutaneous manifestations of Behçet's disease (oral and genital ulcers, erythema nodosum-like lesions) and arthritis. It reduces the frequency and severity of attacks. Thalidomide is an alternative for refractory cases. Corticosteroids are used for ocular and neurological involvement.

questions.q: A 65-year-old man presents with a pearly, telangiectatic nodule on the nose with central ulceration. He has a history of prolonged sun exposure. The most common subtype of basal cell carcinoma associated with this clinical presentation is:
questions.exp: The most common (70%) subtype of BCC is noduloulcerative (rodent ulcer) — a pearly nodule with rolled borders, telangiectasia, and central ulceration. It typically occurs on the face, especially nose and nasolabial area. Morphoeic BCC presents as a scar-like plaque with ill-defined margins; superficial BCC appears as an erythematous scaly plaque on the trunk.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman presents with progressive depigmentation over the hands and face. Woods lamp examination accentuates the lesions. Which investigation distinguishes vitiligo from post-inflammatory hypopigmentation?
questions.exp: Skin biopsy in vitiligo shows complete absence of melanocytes on Fontana-Masson stain and negative DOPA reaction, distinguishing it from post-inflammatory hypopigmentation where melanocytes are present but functionally reduced. Dermoscopy shows white structureless areas in both conditions. Malformed melanosomes are a feature of some genodermatoses.

questions.q: A 42-year-old male presents with fever, generalised lymphadenopathy, and a widespread non-pruritic macular rash including the palms and soles. An annular lesion (condyloma lata) is noted in the perineum. The recommended treatment is:
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM single dose
Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM weekly for 3 weeks
questions.exp: This is secondary syphilis (rash on palms/soles, lymphadenopathy, condylomata lata). Treatment for primary and secondary syphilis is benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM single dose. Three-week course is for late latent/tertiary syphilis. Doxycycline is used in penicillin allergy. Azithromycin is no longer recommended due to resistance.

questions.q: A 28-year-old pregnant woman in her second trimester presents with intensely pruritic urticarial papules and plaques starting on the abdomen with sparing of the umbilicus. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Polymorphic eruption of pregnancy (PEP/PUPPP) is the most common specific dermatosis of pregnancy. It begins in the third trimester (rarely second), starts in striae on the abdomen with characteristic periumbilical sparing, is intensely pruritic, and resolves after delivery. Pemphigoid gestationis also starts periumbilically but causes blistering and is associated with anti-BP180 antibodies.

questions.q: A 50-year-old male presents with a solitary flesh-coloured plaque on the lower leg with satellite nodules and inguinal lymphadenopathy. Biopsy shows large cells with round nuclei and prominent nucleoli with paranuclear dot-like keratin (CK20) positivity on immunohistochemistry. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Merkel cell carcinoma (primary cutaneous neuroendocrine carcinoma) presents as a rapidly growing, flesh-coloured to violaceous nodule on sun-exposed skin. Immunohistochemistry shows paranuclear dot-like positivity for CK20 and positivity for neuroendocrine markers (chromogranin, synaptophysin). CK7 is typically negative (helps distinguish from lung small-cell carcinoma).

questions.q: A 33-year-old woman is referred for laser hair removal. She has Fitzpatrick skin type V. The laser with the best safety profile (lowest risk of dyspigmentation) for this patient is:
questions.exp: Nd:YAG 1064 nm laser is the safest for dark skin types (Fitzpatrick IV-VI) because its longer wavelength is less preferentially absorbed by melanin, reducing the risk of dyspigmentation and burns. Alexandrite and ruby lasers have shorter wavelengths with greater epidermal melanin absorption, making them unsuitable for dark skin. Diode is intermediate.

questions.q: A 25-year-old male with lepromatous leprosy on multidrug therapy develops sudden painful swelling of pre-existing lesions, fever, and neuritis with new skin lesions appearing. This represents:
questions.exp: Type 2 lepra reaction (ENL) occurs in lepromatous and borderline lepromatous leprosy, particularly during MDT. It presents with fever, painful erythematous nodules (ENL), and neuritis. It is an immune complex-mediated (Type III) reaction. Type 1 (reversal reaction) occurs in borderline leprosy and is a Type IV (cell-mediated) reaction. Treatment for ENL is thalidomide or prednisolone.

questions.q: A 60-year-old male with a 20-year history of psoriasis develops psoriatic arthritis with dactylitis and nail changes. The biologic most effective for both skin and joint disease in psoriatic arthritis is:
questions.exp: Anti-TNF-α agents (adalimumab, etanercept, infliximab, certolizumab) have the most robust evidence for both skin and joint manifestations of psoriatic arthritis, including structural inhibition of joint damage. However, secukinumab and ixekizumab (anti-IL-17A) are also highly effective for both. Anti-TNF remains the best-studied class for joint structural outcomes. Ustekinumab has moderate joint efficacy.
